blocks.text: A market trader sells oranges at a fixed price each, plus a ₦50 delivery fee. If a customer paid ₦350 in total, how many oranges did they buy? Every question like this becomes easy once you can solve a linear equation.

blocks.markdown:
A **linear equation** is an equation where the unknown appears only to the power of one. There is no $x^2$, no $x^3$, and no $x$ under a square root.

The equals sign means both sides have exactly the same value. Think of it as a balance scale: whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other, or the scale tips and the equation is no longer true.

blocks.title: Inverse operation
blocks.text: The operation that undoes another. Addition and subtraction undo each other; multiplication and division undo each other. Solving an equation means applying inverse operations until the variable stands alone.

blocks.caption: Our worked example: find the value of x

steps.text: The constant +5 is in the way. Subtract 5 from both sides so the equation stays balanced.
x is multiplied by 3, so divide both sides by 3.
Check by substituting back into the original equation: 3(5) + 5 = 15 + 5 = 20. Correct.

blocks.title: Order matters
blocks.text: Undo addition and subtraction before multiplication and division. This is the reverse of BODMAS — you are unwrapping the expression, so you remove the outermost operation first.

blocks.markdown:
### Variables on both sides

When the unknown appears on both sides, first gather all variable terms on one side and all constants on the other.

For $5x - 3 = 2x + 9$, subtract $2x$ from both sides to get $3x - 3 = 9$, then add 3 to both sides to get $3x = 12$, so $x = 4$.

blocks.caption: Common patterns and the first inverse operation to apply

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Always substitute your answer back into the original equation. It takes ten seconds and catches nearly every sign error, which is the most common way marks are lost on this topic.

points: A linear equation has the unknown raised only to the power of one.
Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other to keep the equation balanced.
Undo addition and subtraction first, then multiplication and division.
When the variable appears on both sides, gather variables on one side and constants on the other.
Always check your answer by substituting it back into the original equation.
